citations.quote: Grouping the sum by the cardinality of $T$, the subsets of cardinality $a$ form a single $S_n$-orbit with stabilizer the ordered block subgroup $S_{\{0,\dots,a-1\}}\times S_{\{a,\dots,n-1\}}\cong S_a\times S_{n-a}$, so the orbit summand is identified with an induced module ([[def-induced-r-linear-g-module-by-h-covariant-functions]]): $$M(W)_n\cong\bigoplus_{a=0}^{n}\operatorname{Ind}_{S_a\times S_{n-a}}^{S_n}\bigl(W_a\boxtimes k\bigr),$$ where $W_a:=W(\{0,\dots,a-1\})$ is the value of the FB-module on an $a$-element set, the first factor acts on $W_a$ through $W$ and the second factor acts trivially, and $\boxtimes$ is the external tensor product of modules for the two direct factors ([[def-outer-induction-product-for-symmetric-group-characters]], [[lem-character-ring-of-a-direct-product-is-the-tensor-product]], [[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]).

(i) For every $k\ge0$ there is an isomorphism of $FS_{n+k}$-modules $$\operatorname{Ind}_{S_n\times S_k}^{S_{n+k}}\bigl(S^\lambda_F\boxtimes F\bigr)\cong\bigoplus_{\mu}S^\mu_F,$$ summed over the partitions $\mu\vdash n+k$ obtained from $\lambda$ by adding one box to each of $k$ different columns (equivalently, $\mu\supseteq\lambda$ and $\mu/\lambda$ is a horizontal $k$-strip).
Consequently, by Maschke's theorem, every finite-dimensional $FS_n$-module is a direct sum of copies of the $S^\lambda_F$;

Let $G$ be a finite group, let $k$ be a field with $\operatorname{char} k \nmid |G|$, let $\rho:G \to \operatorname{GL}(V)$ be a finite-dimensional representation of $G$ over $k$, and let $W \le V$ be a subrepresentation.

A map of FI-modules $\alpha\colon V\to W$ gives $k$-linear maps $\alpha_{\mathbf a\sqcup n}\colon V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n}\to W_{\mathbf a\sqcup n}$ commuting with the $S_n$-actions and with the maps induced by $\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf a}\sqcup f$, hence maps $(\Phi_a\alpha)_n$ of coinvariants commuting with $T$;
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$, let $\mu\vdash n$, and write $\mu=\lambda[n]$ as in [[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]];

Let $W$ be an FB-module over $k$ and let $M(W)$ be the free FI-module of
[[def-free-fi-module-generated-by-an-sm-module]]. Then
$\operatorname{inj-deg}(M(W))=0$, and if $W_i=0$ for all $i>m$ then
$\operatorname{surj-deg}(M(W))\le m$; in particular
$M(m)=M(k[S_m])$ over a nonzero ring $k$ satisfies $\operatorname{inj-deg}(M(m))=0$ and
$\operatorname{stab-deg}(M(m))=m$
([[def-injectivity-surjectivity-and-stability-degree-of-an-fi-module]]).
If moreover $k$ is a field of characteristic $0$ and $\lambda$ is a partition,
then $\operatorname{weight}(M(\lambda))=|\lambda|$
([[def-weight-of-a-characteristic-zero-fi-module]]) and
$\operatorname{stab-deg}(M(\lambda))=\lambda_1$. No choice principle is used.
The **stability degree** is $$\operatorname{stab-deg}(V):=\max\bigl(\operatorname{inj-deg}(V),\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)\bigr).$$ Each of the three is $+\infty$ when no such $s$ exists;

Finite generation of $V$ and pointwise finite generation of the individual $k$-modules $V_S$ are different conditions: the pointwise property is implied by finite generation (as shown below by [[lem-generated-in-degree-d-is-a-quotient-of-free-fi-modules]]) but does not imply it, and no pointwise finite generation or finite-dimensionality is built into either notion.

Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$ ([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]), with free FI-modules $M(m)$ as in [[def-free-fi-module-generated-by-an-sm-module]] and span as in [[def-finite-generation-and-generation-degree-of-an-fi-module]].

derivations.claim: For $n\ge d$ the padded partition $\lambda[n]=(n-m,\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots)$ is obtained from $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots)$ by adding exactly one box in each of the first $n-m$ columns and none elsewhere, because $n-m\ge\lambda_1$; hence $V_{\lambda[n]}$ occurs in $M(\lambda)_n$ with multiplicity one by [F1] and [F2]. For $n\ge d$ let $V(\lambda)_n\subseteq M(\lambda)_n$ be the sum of all $kS_n$-submodules isomorphic to $V_{\lambda[n]}$, and set $V(\lambda)_n:=0$ for $n<d$. As the multiplicity is at most one, this sum is the unique subspace of $M(\lambda)_n$ isomorphic to $V_{\lambda[n]}$, so $V(\lambda)_n\cong V_{\lambda[n]}$ for $n\ge d$. [F1, F2, F3, given]

We show that these subspaces are preserved by transition maps. Let $f\colon[p]\to[q]$ be an injection with $p\ge d$ (if $p<d$, then $V(\lambda)_p=0$ and there is nothing to show), so that $q\ge d$; put $Y:=f_*(V(\lambda)_p)\subseteq M(\lambda)_q$. Since $f_*$ is injective by [F1], $Y\cong V_{\lambda[p]}$. The subspace $Y$ is stable under $H:=\Phi_f(S_p)$, because $f_*\circ\sigma_*=\Phi_f(\sigma)_*\circ f_*$ for all $\sigma\in S_p$, and it is fixed pointwise by $K:=\{\tau\in S_q:\tau|_{f([p])}=\mathrm{id}\}\cong S_{q-p}$, because $\tau\circ f=f$ gives $\tau_*\circ f_*=f_*$ by functoriality. The subgroups $H$ and $K$ commute, $H\times K$ is conjugate in $S_q$ to the standard ordered block subgroup $S_p\times S_{q-p}$, and the pair $(Y,H\text{-action})$ is isomorphic to $(V_{\lambda[p]},S_p\text{-action})$; hence the $S_q$-span $Z$ of $Y$, which is the image of the $S_q$-module map $\operatorname{Ind}_{H\times K}^{S_q}(Y\boxtimes k)\to M(\lambda)_q$, $(u,y)\mapsto u_*y$, is a quotient of $\operatorname{Ind}_{S_p\times S_{q-p}}^{S_q}(V_{\lambda[p]}\boxtimes k)$. [F1, given, algebra]

Every constituent $V_
u$ of $Z$ occurs both in $\operatorname{Ind}_{S_p	imes S_{q-p}}^{S_q}(V_{\lambda[p]} oxtimes k)$ and in $M(\lambda)_q\cong\operatorname{Ind}_{S_m	imes S_{q-m}}^{S_q}(S^\lambda_k oxtimes k)$ by step 1.2; by [F2] this means that $
u\supseteq\lambda[p]$ with $
u_{i+1}\le\lambda[p]_i$ and $
u\supseteq\lambda$ with $
u_{i+1}\le\lambda_i$. Since $\lambda[p]_{i+1}=\lambda_i$ for $i\ge1$, the inequalities $\lambda_i=\lambda[p]_{i+1}\le
u_{i+1}\le\lambda_i$ force $
u_{i+1}=\lambda_i$ for every $i\ge1$, and $
u\vdash q$ gives $
u_1=q-\sum_{i\ge1}\lambda_i=q-m$; hence $
u=\lambda[q]$ is the only possible constituent of $Z$. The multiplicity of $V_{\lambda[q]}$ in $M(\lambda)_q$ is at most one by [F2], so every submodule of $M(\lambda)_q$ all of whose constituents are isomorphic to $V_{\lambda[q]}$ is contained in the isotypic piece $V(\lambda)_q$; in particular $Z\subseteq V(\lambda)_q$, hence $Y\subseteq V(\lambda)_q$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2]

For a finite set $S$ with $|S|=n\ge d$ define $V(\lambda)_S:=\beta_*^{-1}\bigl(V(\lambda)_n\bigr)\subseteq M(\lambda)_S$ for any bijection $\beta\colon S\to[n]$; this does not depend on $\beta$, since any other bijection is $\sigma\circ\beta$ with $\sigma\in S_n$ and $\sigma_*\bigl(V(\lambda)_n\bigr)=V(\lambda)_n$. For $|S|<d$ set $V(\lambda)_S:=0$. If $f\colon S\to T$ is an injection with $|S|=p\ge d$ and $\alpha\colon[p]\to S$, $\beta\colon[q]\to T$ are bijections, write $f=\beta\circ f_0\circ\alpha^{-1}$ with $f_0\colon[p]\to[q]$; then $f_*(V(\lambda)_S)=\beta_*(f_0)_*\alpha_*^{-1}\alpha_*(V(\lambda)_p)=\beta_*(f_0)_*(V(\lambda)_p)\subseteq\beta_*(V(\lambda)_q)=V(\lambda)_T$ by step 1.2, using the functoriality of $M(\lambda)$. Hence $V(\lambda)$ is a sub-FI-module of $M(\lambda)$ with the stated values. [F1, given, step 1.2, step 2.1]

For $n\ge d$ and any injection $f\colon[d]\to[n]$, the map $f_*\colon M(\lambda)_d\to M(\lambda)_n$ is injective by [F1], so its restriction $f_*(V(\lambda)_d)$ is nonzero because $V(\lambda)_d\cong V_{\lambda[d]}\ne0$ [F3], and it lies in $V(\lambda)_n$ by step 1.2. Every injection $[d]\to[n]$ equals $\sigma\circ f$ for some $\sigma\in S_n$, and $(\sigma\circ f)_*=\sigma_*\circ f_*$, so $\operatorname{span}_{V(\lambda)}(V(\lambda)_d)_n$ is the $S_n$-span of $f_*(V(\lambda)_d)$: a nonzero $kS_n$-submodule of the irreducible $V(\lambda)_n$ [F3], hence all of $V(\lambda)_n$. For $n<d$ both sides are $0$, so $\operatorname{span}_{V(\lambda)}(V(\lambda)_{\le d})=V(\lambda)$; thus $V(\lambda)$ is generated in degree $\le d$ by [F7], and as $V(\lambda)_n=0$ for $n<d$ with $V(\lambda)_d\ne0$, its generation degree is exactly $d$. A finite $k$-basis of the finite-dimensional $V(\lambda)_d$ generates all of it, so this FI-module is finitely generated. [F1, F3, F7, step 1.2, step 3.1]

For $n\ge d$ the value $V(\lambda)_n\cong V_{\lambda[n]}$ is irreducible of label $\lambda[n]$, and the tail label has $|\lambda|=n-(n-m)=m$; a subquotient of an irreducible module is $0$ or the module itself, so $V(\lambda)_n$ is the only constituent of itself, its label being $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|=m$ ([[def-weight-of-a-characteristic-zero-fi-module]]). For $n<d$ the value is $0$. Hence $\operatorname{weight}(V(\lambda))=m$, the supremum being attained in every degree $n\ge d$. [given, F3, step 3.1]

By step 3.1 the module $V(\lambda)$ is a sub-FI-module of $M(\lambda)$. For all $a,n$ the inclusion $V(\lambda)_{\mathbf a\sqcup n}\subseteq M(\lambda)_{\mathbf a\sqcup n}$ induces an injective map $\Phi_aV(\lambda)_n\to\Phi_aM(\lambda)_n$ because $k$ contains $\mathbb Q$ [F4], and by naturality of $T$ these maps commute with the transition maps. If $T\colon\Phi_aM(\lambda)_n\to\Phi_aM(\lambda)_{n+1}$ is injective, then $T\colon\Phi_aV(\lambda)_n\to\Phi_aV(\lambda)_{n+1}$ is injective as well; since $\operatorname{inj-deg}(M(\lambda))=0$ by [F6], the latter holds for all $n\ge0$, so $\operatorname{inj-deg}(V(\lambda))=0$. [F4, F6, step 3.1]

Let $\mu:=\lambda[d]\vdash d$, so that $\mu_1=d-m=\lambda_1$. By step 4.1 the module $V(\lambda)$ is generated in degree $\le d$, so the evaluation map $e\colon M(V(\lambda)_d)\to V(\lambda)$ is surjective by [F7]; since $V(\lambda)_d\cong V_\mu$ is irreducible, $M(V(\lambda)_d)\cong M(\mu)$ by the additivity of $M$ in [F1]. For any surjection $q\colon U\twoheadrightarrow W$ of FI-modules and all $a,n$, the map $\Phi_a(q)_n$ is surjective because $\Phi_a$ preserves surjections [F4], and naturality gives $T_W\circ\Phi_a(q)_n=\Phi_a(q)_{n+1}\circ T_U$; hence $T_U$ surjective implies $T_W$ surjective, so $\operatorname{surj-deg}(W)\le\operatorname{surj-deg}(U)$ (Lemma 3.1.6 of the source). Applying this to $e$ and using [F6], $\operatorname{surj-deg}(V(\lambda))\le\operatorname{surj-deg}(M(\mu))=\mu_1=\lambda_1$. [F1, F4, F6, F7, step 4.1]

Suppose $\lambda_1\ge1$. With $a:=m$ one has $a+\lambda_1=d$, so by [F5] applied with $n:=d$, $a:=m$ and $\mu:=\lambda[d]$, whose first part is $\mu_1=d-m=\lambda_1$, the coinvariants $\bigl(V(\lambda)_d\bigr)_{S_{\lambda_1}}$ are isomorphic to $V_\lambda\ne0$, and by [F4] they are $\Phi_mV(\lambda)_{\lambda_1}$ (under the identification of the set $\mathbf m\sqcup\lambda_1$ of size $d$ with $[d]$, which is immaterial because conjugate subgroups have isomorphic coinvariants); moreover $\Phi_mV(\lambda)_{\lambda_1-1}=\bigl(V(\lambda)_{d-1}\bigr)_{S_{\lambda_1-1}}=0$, since $V(\lambda)$ vanishes below $d$ by step 1.1. Hence $T\colon\Phi_mV(\lambda)_{\lambda_1-1}\to\Phi_mV(\lambda)_{\lambda_1}$ has zero source and nonzero target, so it is not surjective and $\operatorname{surj-deg}(V(\lambda))\ge\lambda_1$; with step 5.1, $\operatorname{surj-deg}(V(\lambda))=\lambda_1$, and with step 4.3, $\operatorname{stab-deg}(V(\lambda))=\max(0,\lambda_1)=\lambda_1$. If $\lambda_1=0$, then $\lambda=\varnothing$, $m=d=0$ and $M(\varnothing)=M(k)$ has all values $k$ and all transition maps isomorphisms by [F1], so $V(\varnothing)=M(\varnothing)$ and $\operatorname{inj-deg}=\operatorname{surj-deg}=\operatorname{stab-deg}=0=\lambda_1$. [F1, F4, F5, step 1.1, step 3.1, step 4.3, step 5.1]

Steps 1.1, 1.2, 2.1 and 3.1 construct the sub-FI-module $V(\lambda)\subseteq M(\lambda)$ with values $V_{\lambda[n]}$ for $n\ge d$ and $0$ otherwise; step 4.1 shows that its generation degree is exactly $d$; step 4.2 gives $\operatorname{weight}(V(\lambda))=m$; and steps 4.3–6.1 give $\operatorname{inj-deg}(V(\lambda))=0$ and $\operatorname{surj-deg}(V(\lambda))=\operatorname{stab-deg}(V(\lambda))=\lambda_1$. The only selections made are bijections between finite sets, and the value at each finite set was shown to be independent of the selection, so no choice principle is used. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 4.2, step 4.3, step 5.1, step 6.1] ∎

boundaries.evidence: step 1.1: for lambda = emptyset the padding is emptyset[n] = (n) and M(emptyset) = M(k); the empty partition family is the constant module on trivial labels.
step 6.1: the case lambda_1 = 0 is exactly lambda = emptyset and is dispatched there, where m = d = 0 and all transition maps are isomorphisms.
step 4.1: a single injection f: [d] -> [n] suffices for generation, since f_*(V(lambda)_d) is nonzero and its S_n-span is all of V(lambda)_n.
step 2.1: the interlacing argument is run at p = d, the boundary where lambda[p] = (lambda_1, lambda_1, lambda_2, ...), and rules out every other shape nu.
step 6.1: the sharpness witness sits at the endpoint a = m, lambda_1, where Phi_m V(lambda)_{lambda_1-1} = 0 while Phi_m V(lambda)_{lambda_1} = V_lambda is nonzero.
step 3.1: the value V(lambda)_S is defined through any bijection S -> [n] and shown independent of the bijection, so no selection of identifications affects the construction.

boundaries.reason: The proposition asserts existence of a sub-FI-module and computes three invariants; no if-and-only-if is claimed.
No converse characterisation of all modules realising the padded family is asserted.

risk_review.notes: Read every numbered step and fourteen supplier statements. The multiplicity-one isotypic subspace in M(lambda) is canonical. Images under injections are fixed by the complement symmetric group, so their span is an induced quotient; the two horizontal-strip constraints force every constituent to have exactly tail lambda. Transport to all finite sets is independent of bijections. Nonzero injective image from first rank d generates each irreducible value, and a finite basis at d gives finite generation and its exact degree. Weight is the tail size m. Exact coinvariants inherit injectivity, evaluation from M(lambda[d]) bounds surjectivity by lambda_1, and zero-to-nonzero coinvariants prove sharpness. Empty lambda gives the constant module with all degrees zero. Accept correction from full partition size to tail size and the finite basis argument.

derivations.claim: The $F^mV$ are sub-FI-modules with $F^mV\subseteq F^{m+1}V$, $V=\bigcup_mF^mV$, and each $F^mV$ is generated in degree $\le m$. [F1, given]

If every constituent of every $(G_m)_n$ has padding tail first row $\le s$, then so does every constituent of every $V_n$: let $V(\lambda)_n\cong P/Q$ be a constituent of $V_n$ and lift a $k$-basis of the finite-dimensional module $P/Q$ to elements of $P$ and take the span of their finite $S_n$-orbits, giving a finite-dimensional $kS_n$-submodule $P_0\subseteq P$ with $P_0+Q=P$; then $P_0/(P_0\cap Q)\cong P/Q$, and $P_0\subseteq(F^MV)_n$ for some $M$ because a finite basis of $P_0$ lies in a common filtration term. Intersecting the filtration with $P_0$ gives finite-dimensional successive factors embedding in $(G_m)_n$. Maschke splits this finite filtration, so every simple constituent of $P_0$ occurs in one of those factors; hence $V(\lambda)_n$ is a constituent of some $(G_m)_n$. [F1, F6, given, algebra]
Suppose $m\le s$. Then every constituent $V_\mu$ of $H_m$ has $\mu_1\le m\le s$ because $\mu\vdash m$. [given]

Suppose $m\ge s+1$ and set $\overline V:=V/F^{m-1}V$ and $a_0:=m-s-1\ge0$. As a quotient of $V$, the FI-module $\overline V$ has $\operatorname{surj-deg}(\overline V)\le s$ by [F2], so $T\colon\Phi_{a_0}(\overline V)_s\to\Phi_{a_0}(\overline V)_{s+1}$ is surjective. Its domain is $(\overline V_{m-1})_{S_s}=0$ because $\overline V_{m-1}=0$, and its target is $(\overline V_m)_{S_{s+1}}$; also $\overline V_m=V_m/\operatorname{span}_V(V_{<m})_m\cong H_m$ by the second isomorphism theorem. Hence $(H_m)_{S_{s+1}}=0$, and for every constituent $V_\mu$ of $H_m$ the coinvariants $(V_\mu)_{S_{s+1}}$ are a subquotient of $(H_m)_{S_{s+1}}$, hence vanish; by [F3] applied with $a=m-(s+1)$, so that $m-a=s+1$, this says $s+1>\mu_1$, i.e. $\mu_1\le s$. [F2, F3, F5, given]

The quotient $G_m$ is generated in degree $\le m$ and has $(G_m)_i=0$ for $i<m$, so by [F2] the evaluation map $M(H_m)\twoheadrightarrow G_m$ is surjective. Hence every constituent of $(G_m)_n$ is a constituent of $M(H_m)_n$. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

Every constituent of $M(H_m)_n$ has padding tail first row $\le s$: let $V(\lambda)_n\cong P/Q$ be a constituent of $M(H_m)_n$ and choose $x\in P\setminus Q$; the $S_n$-orbit span $X$ of $x$ is finite-dimensional, and $X/(X\cap Q)$ is a nonzero submodule of the simple $V(\lambda)_n$, hence isomorphic to it, so $V(\lambda)_n$ is a constituent of $X$. Since $X$ lies in the direct sum $ igoplus_{T\subseteq[n],|T|=m}H_m(T)$ over finitely many $T$, after transporting by bijections $[m]	o T$ for these finitely many subsets, the projections of $X$ to the summands $H_m(T)$ generate a finite-dimensional $kS_m$-submodule $N\subseteq H_m$ with $X\subseteq M(N)_n$; so $V(\lambda)_n$ is a constituent of $M(N)_n$. By [F6] write $N\cong igoplus_\mu V_\mu^{\oplus c_\mu}$ (finite sum over partitions $\mu\vdash m$ with $c_\mu
e0$); every such $V_\mu$ is a constituent of $H_m$, so $\mu_1\le s$ by steps 1.3 and 1.4. By [F6] $M(N)\cong igoplus_\mu M(V_\mu)^{\oplus c_\mu}$, and by [F4] every constituent $V_
u$ of $M(V_\mu)_n$ satisfies $
u_2\le\mu_1\le s$; a constituent of a finite direct sum is a constituent of one summand, so for the constituent $V(\lambda)_n\cong V_{\lambda[n]}$ of $M(N)_n$ we get $\lambda_1=(\lambda[n])_2\le s$. [F1, F4, F6, step 1.4]

For a finite set $S$ with $|S|=m\le N$ and a bijection $\beta\colon[m]\to S$ one has $V_S=\beta_*(V_{[m]})\subseteq\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)_S$, so $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)\supseteq V_{\le N}$ and therefore $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)=V$; thus $V$ is finitely generated. [F1, F2, given]

Returning to $(\Rightarrow)$: for every $a$, the exactness of $\Phi_a$ over the characteristic-zero field $k$ gives an exact sequence $0\to\Phi_a(K)\to\Phi_a(M)\to\Phi_a(V)\to0$ by [F6]. The module $M$ is a finite direct sum of copies of the free modules $M(i)$, each of injectivity degree $0$ by [F4], so $T\colon\Phi_a(M)_n\to\Phi_a(M)_{n+1}$ is injective for all $n$ by [F6] and [F7]; and $T\colon\Phi_a(K)_n\to\Phi_a(K)_{n+1}$ is surjective for $n\ge r$ by [F3]. Hence $T\colon\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(V)_{n+1}$ is injective for $n\ge r$: a lift $\tilde x\in\Phi_a(M)_n$ of $x$ with $Tx=0$ has $T\tilde x$ in the image of $\Phi_a(K)$, so $T\tilde x=T\tilde y$ for some $\tilde y\in\Phi_a(K)_n$, and injectivity on $\Phi_a(M)$ gives $\tilde x=\tilde y$, whence $x=0$. Therefore $\operatorname{inj-deg}(V)\le r$ by [F7], and $\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)\le\max(g,r)$ since $\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)\le g$. [F3, F4, F6, F7, step 1.1]

Under the assumption of step 1.1 the weight is finite, indeed $\operatorname{weight}(V)\le g$ by [F3] over the characteristic-zero field $k$, and $\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)\le\max(g,r)<\infty$ by step 2.1. By [F8] the sequence $(V_n,\varphi_n)$ is uniformly representation stable, with stable range $n\ge g+\max(g,r)$. [F3, F8, step 2.1]

Steps 1.1, 2.1 and 3.1 prove that finite generation implies uniform representation stability (through finiteness of stability degree and weight and the preceding proposition), and step 1.2 proves the converse; hence for an FI-module with finite-dimensional values over a characteristic-zero field the two properties are equivalent. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎
